title: Introduce drift-anchored smoke-eval with per-prompt failback and granular gating
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add a lightweight drift-anchored smoke evaluation runner and CI hook that triggers per-prompt severity checks and automated failback to fallback model variants when anchors degrade. Includes telemetry and docs update.
description: Context: We need a lightweight, fast smoke evaluation that can run in CI and short-circuit regressions at a prompt-set level without waiting for full-scale evals. Motivation: recent incidents showed slow detection of prompt-specific regressions causing downstream rollback delays. This PR introduces a drift-anchored smoke-eval framework which anchors prompt severity to historical embeddings and scalar metrics, runs a compact probe suite in CI, and wires automatic failback policies that can recommend a fallback model variant or trigger a canary rollback if thresholds are exceeded. What this change does: 1) Adds a new smoke runner module eval_harness.runners.drift_anchor_smoke which computes per-prompt anchor scores using embedding-distance baselines plus a lightweight categorical-quality metric. 2) Introduces a CI hook eval_harness.ci.hooks.DriftAnchorSmokeHook that runs on PRs touching prompt sets or model adapters and produces a single pass/fail signal plus an HTML summary artifact. 3) Implements a per-prompt severity taxonomy and configurable thresholds (low/medium/high) backed by historical percentiles (90/95/99) so small noisy regressions are attenuated. 4) Adds an automated failback shim that suggests fallback model variants (fallbacks derived from model catalog metadata) and can mark PRs with suggested action labels (ci/failback-suggested). 5) Instrumentation: new telemetry metrics eval.smoke.anchor_score.*, eval.smoke.failed_prompts, and eval.smoke.recommended_fallback stored via the existing metrics client. 6) Tests: unit tests for anchor scoring logic, integration test for the hook, and a smoke e2e that runs against the local simulator. 7) Docs: quickstart snippets and troubleshooting runbook under docs/smoke-evals/drift-anchored.md. Rollout plan: merge into main behind a feature flag smoke_evals.drift_anchor.enabled=false by default, enable for canary projects via Linear ENG-2431 and then broader rollout after 2 weeks of telemetry. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of anchor scoring and thresholds. - [x] CI hook producing artifact and non-blocking default behavior. - [x] Unit and integration tests. - [x] Telemetry emission. - [x] Docs and runbook. - [x] Linked Linear tasks created. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is non-blocking; repositories not opting in will see no change. Known limitations: the initial anchor method uses off-the-shelf embeddings and can be sensitive to tokenizer changes; future work includes embedding-stable hashing and cohort-aware baselines. Related: ENG-2431 (drift detection platform), ENG-2507 (ci gating UX).

review_comments: Rosa Almeida: Nice work, this addresses the slow detection issue we saw in the incident. Two asks before approving: add a metric tag for prompt_set_id and ensure the hook is opt-in by default.
Maya Patel: Thanks! Added prompt_set_id tag to the telemetry and wrapped the hook behind smoke_evals.drift_anchor.enabled=false in defaults.yaml. Also added notes about opting in in the docs.
Liam Chen: Can we avoid embedding compute in PR CI for large prompt sets? Suggest sampling and async artifact production for >500 prompts.

Maya Patel: Implemented a sampling heuristic that samples by shard and emits a 'sampled=true' tag when sampling is applied. Async artifact fallback is also implemented for larger runs, artifact will be produced in background and CI shows partial result.
Ethan Ross: Unit test flaked on CI run due to random seed; please make deterministic.
Maya Patel: Fixed seed in test_drift_anchor_score and added a deterministic fixture for embeddings.
Rosa Almeida: Approving after fixes. Please add a short runbook step to the incident playbook about interpreting anchor_score spikes.
Maya Patel: Added runbook snippet and example alert query to docs/smoke-evals/drift-anchored.md and the SLO playbook.

notes: This PR is intentionally conservative in default behavior. The main benefit is early, prompt-specific detection in PRs and lightweight, explainable suggestions for failback. Next steps: add cohort-aware anchor baselines, integrate with rollout service for automated canary rollback, and expose per-prompt historical time series in the console.
short_summary: Adds a CI smoke-eval hook that anchors per-prompt severity to historical baselines, emits telemetry, and suggests fallback models when prompt regressions exceed configurable thresholds. Default opt-in is false; rollout planned via canary projects.
impact_statement: Operational: improves time-to-detection for prompt-specific regressions and provides automated failback suggestions. Risk: initial sensitivity to embedding changes; mitigated by conservative thresholds and non-blocking default.
